description.text: Protagonist Therapeutics, Inc. (referred to as “Protagonist,” the “Company,” “we,” “our” or “us”) is an integrated discovery and development company with a validated technology platform. Our programs fall into three broad therapeutic areas: (i) inflammation and immunology (“I&I”), (ii) hematology and (iii) metabolic diseases. Our aim is to develop medicines for biologically and commercially validated targets which demonstrate a strong differentiation compared to existing therapies.

about.description_short: Protagonist Therapeutics is a biopharmaceutical company built on a proprietary peptide technology platform that has now produced two FDA-approved, first-in-class medicines, generating royalties and milestones from global commercial partnerships with Johnson and Johnson and Takeda Pharmaceutical Company Limited. ICOTYDE (icotrokinra), licensed to Johnson & Johnson company Janssen Biotech, Inc., is the first and only targeted oral peptide that precisely blocks the Interleukin-23 receptor. ICOTYDE was launched in the U.S. in March 2026 for the treatment of moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis in adults and pediatric patients 12 years of age or older and is in Phase 3 development for psoriatic arthritis, ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease.

analysis_md:
# PTGX — Protagonist Therapeutics, Inc
v5 run, 2026-10-20. Price $139.11 (nasdaq_quote_api), market cap $8.843B — in scope under $40B.

All figures below are copied from dcf_numbers.json, ttm.json, financials_history.csv, or fundamentals.json — none are recomputed. Partner economics and 2026 events are from cited company reporting (Q1/Q2 2026 results and the 5 Aug 2026 corporate presentation).

## What it is
Clinical/commercial-stage peptide biotech built on a constrained-peptide platform. Two partnered, first-in-class assets now carry the value: ICOTYDE (icotrokinra, oral IL-23R antagonist, partnered with Johnson & Johnson), FDA-approved March 2026 for moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis, paying 6–10% royalties; and rusfertide (subcutaneous hepcidin mimetic for polycythemia vera, partnered with Takeda), for which Protagonist opted out of US profit-sharing in April 2026 in exchange for royalty economics of 14–29% plus milestones. Wholly-owned follow-ons: PN-881 (oral IL-17A/F), PN-477 (triple GLP-1/GIP/GCG), PN-8047 (oral hepcidin). The company sells no product itself — revenue is collaboration, milestone and (starting 2026) royalty income.

## Owner's earnings
Owner's earnings here means OCF − capex − SBC. The annual record is a milestone sawtooth, not a business run-rate:

- FY2023: revenue $60,000,000; OCF −$70,236,000; capex $609,000; SBC $29,293,000 → OE −$100,138,000 (−$1.76/share)
- FY2024: revenue $434,433,000; OCF $184,152,000; capex $1,355,000; SBC $37,554,000 → OE $145,243,000 ($2.23/share) — the spike year
- FY2025: revenue $46,016,000; OCF $57,671,000; capex $1,590,000; SBC $45,974,000 → OE $10,107,000 ($0.16/share)
- OE positive in only 2 of the last 5 fiscal years (dcf_numbers.json). The maintenance definition (NI-based) for FY2025 prints −$86,898,000 against the conservative +$10,107,000 — working-capital swings dominate the gap; the OCF-based conservative series is the one used throughout.
- The engine's normalized base (median of last 3 FY OE/share) is $0.16/share. It is arithmetically correct and economically useless: the three years it medians are −$1.76, +$2.23 and +$0.16.

**Base used = TTM owner's earnings through Q2 2026, from ttm.py (filing-direct):**
- OCF: FY $57,671,000 − prior YTD $96,583,000 + current YTD $170,109,000 = **TTM $131,197,000**
- Capex: FY $1,590,000 − prior YTD $1,358,000 + current YTD $383,000 = **TTM $615,000**
- SBC: FY $45,974,000 − prior YTD $24,714,000 + current YTD $28,556,000 = **TTM $49,816,000**
- Shares (current-YTD weighted diluted): **70,818,718**
- **TTM OE total $80,766,000 → base OE/share $1.14** (base_source: ttm_json)
- Honest caveat on that base: TTM revenue is $281,992,000 (fundamentals.json) and Q2 2026 revenue of $213.47M was driven by Takeda opt-out economics, on top of a $50M J&J ICOTYDE approval milestone in Q1 2026 — the TTM base is itself milestone-heavy, not recurring royalty run-rate. Both defensible bases are dwarfed by the price (see method range).

## Moat: 4/10 — narrow, partner-held
Justification: Two first-in-class partnered approvals (icotrokinra/ICOTYDE oral IL-23R with J&J, rusfertide hepcidin mimetic with Takeda) and a validated oral-peptide platform, but Protagonist owns no commercial channel, keeps only 6–10% royalties on its largest asset, depends on partners for execution, and ROIC was negative in four of the last six fiscal years (only the 2024 milestone spike year was positive at +43.1%).
- FOR: First-in-class approved peptides: ICOTYDE is the first FDA-approved targeted oral IL-23R peptide (Mar 2026); rusfertide is a first-in-class hepcidin mimetic for polycythemia vera; platform validated by J&J and Takeda partnerships — $912.5M in upfront/milestone payments earned through June 2026 per the Aug 2026 corporate presentation; patent-protected royalty streams are near-100% margin and require almost no capex (TTM capex $615,000); pipeline breadth from the same platform: PN-881 (oral IL-17A/F), PN-477 (triple GLP-1/GIP/GCG), PN-8047 (oral hepcidin).
- AGAINST: No commercial capability — opted out of US rusfertide profit-sharing (Apr 2026); partners control pricing, launch and sales execution; thin economics on the biggest asset: only 6–10% royalties on icotrokinra despite >$10B claimed peak potential; ROIC history is negative in 4 of last 6 years (roic_proxy from fundamentals.json: 2020 −31.4%, 2021 −56.4%, 2022 −115.5%, 2023 −49.3%, 2024 +43.1%, 2025 −25.7%) — no through-cycle compounding record; revenue is milestone-driven and concentrated in two partners; heavy SBC: $49,816,000 TTM and rising every year, diluted share count growing ~9.0%/yr. Gross margin is not reported (collaboration revenue carries no COGS line in fundamentals.json), so the moat case rests on the ROIC series and the royalty structure, not margins.
- A 4 gives CAP = 7.2 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 7.2 years, 15-year projection. A moat of 7+ would need ROIC sustained above the cost of capital through a cycle; the filed history shows the opposite outside one milestone year.

## DCF — v5 final run (2026-10-20)
Growth-start sanity check and recalibration (written reason): the engine's blended start is 4.96%, built from revenue CAGRs (5y 9.96%, 3y 20.07%) and a latest-FY revenue YoY of −89.4% — every one of those inputs straddles the FY2024 milestone spike, so none of them describes the forward economics. The forward story is a royalty ramp off a near-zero recurring base (ICOTYDE launched 2026; rusfertide royalties at 14–29%), plus contracted milestones, minus R&D growing into PN-881/PN-477. Scenario starts were therefore set by offsets (−0.12 / −0.02 / +0.10 / +0.20 / +0.30 vs g_base) to −7.04 / +2.96 / **+14.96** / +24.96 / +34.96%. That the bull and super-bull starts sit far above the (artefact-depressed) blend is deliberate and written here; even the super-bull start produces an IV less than a third of the price. Probabilities 10/25/30/25/10; OE multipliers 0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25.

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | Story | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 10% | −7.04% | 0.75 | Royalty ramp disappoints; milestones dry up; R&D keeps rising | $4.84 | 2.89% |
| Bear | 25% | 2.96% | 0.90 | Modest royalties, pipeline spend absorbs them | $8.57 | 3.27% |
| Base | 30% | 14.96% | 1.00 | Royalties ramp through the CAP; milestones continue at a lower cadence | $14.97 | 3.99% |
| Bull | 25% | 24.96% | 1.10 | ICOTYDE and rusfertide track toward partner peak-sales claims | $23.71 | 4.99% |
| Super bull | 10% | 34.96% | 1.25 | Both assets blockbuster; PN-881/PN-477 add a second wave | $38.33 | 6.57% |

- **Probability-weighted: IV@15% $16.88 (−87.9% vs price), IV@12% $22.95, IV@10% $29.78, weighted IRR 4.24%, base-case IRR 3.99%**
- **Tier by numbers: D** (bear D, bull D — no band ambiguity). Diagnostics (dcf_numbers.json): OE yield 0.82%, terminal value 21.0% of IV@15%, scenario spread 7.93x, 9.6 months since FY end, net-debt ratio not computed (see DEBT_TAGS_BLANK).
- Hurdle prices: clears 15% at $16.88, 20% at $11.49, 25% at $8.58 — against a $139.11 price.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **STALE_FY** (FY ended 9.6 months ago): resolved by construction — the base is the TTM figure from ttm.py through Q2 2026, legs quoted above.
- **DILUTION** (share count +9.0%/yr): real and SBC-driven — SBC rose $29,293,000 (2023) → $37,554,000 (2024) → $45,974,000 (2025) → $49,816,000 TTM, and the diluted count rose from 63,573,048 (FY2025) to a TTM denominator of 70,818,718. Already deducted via the −5pp growth adjustment in the blend; a $300M buyback was authorized 8 Sep 2026 (company announcement) but no repurchase has yet offset the SBC issuance in the filed counts.
- **BASIS_BREAK_SUSPECT**: no divestiture, M&A or restatement — the >60% revenue swings are milestone/license lumpiness in a collaboration-revenue model: $60,000,000 (2023) → $434,433,000 (2024) → $46,016,000 (2025). Consequence: no CAGR straddling FY2024 is trusted; scenario starts were set from launch-ramp economics instead (see DCF section).
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (2024, 2025): 2025 — net income −$130,149,000 vs OCF +$57,671,000: the loss carries $45,974,000 of non-cash SBC that OCF adds back, plus working-capital effects; 2024 — net income $275,188,000 vs OCF $184,152,000 in the year $434,433,000 of collaboration revenue was recognized ahead of its cash collection. The base is built on OCF throughout, so neither accrual spike nor accrual loss contaminates it; the divergence is the milestone model's accounting, named here, not a hidden one-off.
- **SHARES_FALLBACK** (2016–2019): those history years use the basic/outstanding counts recorded in the shares_tag column (FALLBACK:CommonStockSharesOutstanding) — per-share history there is approximate. It does not touch the base: the last-3-FY years and the TTM denominator are all filed diluted counts.
- **DEBT_TAGS_BLANK**: no debt tag reports for FY2025, so the engine's net debt is unknown, not zero. Balance sheet from the filing (financials_history.csv, FY2025): cash and equivalents $128,390,000 (cash only — marketable securities are inside total assets, not broken out in the CSV), total assets $668,188,000, total liabilities $53,481,000, equity $614,707,000, operating lease liabilities $10,323,000, and no borrowings line. Company reporting puts cash, equivalents and marketable securities at $849.5M at Q2 2026. This is an effectively debt-free, cash-rich balance sheet; leverage is not the risk — valuation is.
- **IRR_AT_FLOOR** (super bear only, in the final run): the super-bear IRR of 2.89% sits within 0.5pp of the 2.5% terminal rate, so it reads "at most ~3%" rather than a precise figure. The weighted IRR (4.24%) is off the floor, and no scenario comes within 8pp of the 15% hurdle, so the floor does not change the verdict.
- **LOW_OE_YIELD** (0.82% on the TTM base): agreed — the valuation rests almost entirely on future royalty growth that has not yet printed as recurring cash flow. That is precisely why the tier is D and confidence is low.
- **WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD** (7.93x): real — outcomes range from royalty disappointment to two blockbusters. Confidence is low (never high with this flag), and the verdict is sized to the conservative end: even the super-bull IV@15% of $38.33 is 72% below the price.

## My thoughts / overlay
- Method range: on the preliminary median-base run (base $0.16/share, default offsets) the weighted IV@15% was $1.55 with a weighted IRR of 2.65%; on the final TTM base with launch-ramp growth it is $16.88 at 4.24%. The methods span an order of magnitude and every one of them lands in Tier D — the range is the finding, and it does not straddle any hurdle.
- What the price is paying for: at $139.11 and $8.843B market cap, the market is capitalizing the partners' peak-sales claims (>$10B for icotrokinra, $1–2B for rusfertide, per the Aug 2026 corporate presentation) at royalty rates of 6–10% and 14–29%, plus the early pipeline — a decade of near-flawless partner execution, before it has printed as recurring cash. The filed OE record ($80,766,000 TTM, milestone-dominated) supports a small fraction of that.
- The balance sheet is genuinely strong ($849.5M cash and securities at Q2 2026 per company reporting, no borrowings, a $300M buyback authorized) — downside protection for the company, not for a buyer at this price: cash is roughly a tenth of the market cap.
- This is a royalty-optionality story, and owner's-earnings DCF on filed cash flows is the wrong instrument to price optionality generously — but it is the instrument of this sweep, and on it there is no version of the numbers that clears even 10%.

## Final verdict
- **Final tier: D** (weighted IRR 4.24% on the TTM base; bear and bull both D)
- Confidence: **Low** (WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD 7.93x, milestone-dominated TTM base, binary partner execution ahead)
- One-liner: Real platform, two approved partnered drugs, moat 4/10 — but at $139.11 the price capitalizes blockbuster royalties a decade out: TTM OE is $1.14/share, weighted IRR 4.24% and weighted IV@15% $16.88; it would need to trade near $16.88 to clear 15%.
